newsitem.title: NIGERIA: U.S. drugs team looks at Nigerian efforts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drugs team looks at Nigerian efforts.

text.p: A team of United States anti-drug officials arrived in Nigeria on Monday to look at the country's efforts to combat the narcotics trade.
"The team will be here for the next three days and meet with the Nigerian drug agency and special government adviser on drugs," said a government spokesman in the capital Abuja.
"They will also meet with the finance minister to look at the ways in which Nigeria has been able to cut down on frauds which are often associated with drugs."
The government's special adviser on drugs and financial crimes last week welcomed the visit as a chance to prove that Nigeria is serious about beating the drugs trade.
In May Nigeria rejected a U.S. report which said the West African country was not doing enough.
Nigeria does not produce heroin or cocaine but has a reputation as a major transit centre point and many Nigerian couriers are serving prison terms abroad.
Nigeria has been "decertified" by the U.S. twice since 1994, a measure that blocks economic aid and which Washington takes when dissatisfied with a country's effort in the drug war.
Nigeria's relations with the U.S. have been sour since 1993 when the army annulled a presidential poll to end military rule.
